tone_patterns: Formal, governance-oriented tone emphasizing control, oversight, and accountability
Risk-centric framing that links sustainability risks to financial impacts and decision-making
Process-driven language highlighting methodologies, checks, approvals, and monitoring cadence
Balanced, explanatory tone that defines concepts before describing controls and responsibilities
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short definitional paragraph that characterizes the risk category and why it matters (including financial statement linkage)
Transitions into a segmentation paragraph that states the risk management approach differs by business verticals
Uses repeated sub-sections per vertical: (a) purpose/mandate, (b) governance/ownership, (c) tools and inputs, (d) controls and approvals, (e) monitoring and reporting
Includes role-based paragraphs that distinguish responsibilities across lines of defence (business vs risk function vs credit review)
Uses dense, multi-sentence paragraphs to describe end-to-end workflow steps (assessment → due diligence → approval → monitoring)
Adds an illustrative callout-style mini-section to show how the process works in practice, followed by a list of assessment factors
heading_patterns: Numbered subsection heading combining section number and descriptive title (e.g., 'X.X [topic]')
Vertical-specific headings presented as a numbered list of business areas, implying a structured walkthrough
Intermittent short label headings (e.g., a brief 'process' label) used to introduce a practical example or methodology summary
Continuation across pages with headings reintroduced to maintain reader orientation
table_patterns: No tables present in the excerpt; content that could be tabular is instead presented as bullet lists and procedural narrative
Where structured information is needed, the report favors enumerated lists over tabular layouts in this section
figure_or_diagram_patterns: No explicit figures/diagrams shown; a 'process in action' style callout functions as a pseudo-diagram via structured text and factor listing
Methodology description uses a composite-factor list to emulate a framework visualization without graphics
pdf_layout_patterns: Two-page spread with consistent footer containing report title and page number
Section header/label repeated near the bottom of the page to reinforce the current disclosure area
Use of whitespace and line breaks to separate verticals and improve scanability
Bulleted lists used for both (a) enumerating business verticals and (b) listing principles/exclusions; bullets are vertically spaced for readability
Page break occurs mid-section; the next page resumes with continued numbering to preserve continuity
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses definitional language to clarify risk categories and scope (value chain framing)
Employs governance and policy terminology (frameworks, policies, standards, approvals, exceptions) to evidence control environment
Uses cautious, compliance-aligned phrasing (e.g., responsibilities, oversight, independent confirmation, consultation as needed)
Describes monitoring using periodic reporting cadence and references to risk appetite and stress testing as control mechanisms
Explains screening/assessment inputs by referencing internal and external information sources in an abstract, non-promotional manner
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented through named control activities (due diligence, checks and balances, independent review) rather than quantitative results
Methodology credibility is supported by listing representative assessment factors (environmental and social dimensions) and indicating composite scoring
Assurance-by-design approach: highlights separation of duties and independent confirmation steps
Monitoring evidence is framed as recurring reporting outputs and defined metrics, without embedding detailed figures in the narrative
section_specific_observations: The section is organized around downstream/value-chain risk and then decomposed by business vertical, creating a repeatable template for multi-division organizations
The narrative integrates sustainability risk into existing credit and transaction processes rather than presenting it as a standalone ESG workflow
A dedicated mini-block is used to translate policy language into operational steps and factor-based scoring logic
Lists of principles/exclusions are used to explain product- or model-specific risk mitigation logic in a structured, reader-friendly way
things_to_avoid_copying: Any company name, brand, or business unit naming conventions unique to the reference organization
Any references to specific frameworks, policies, or acronyms that are proprietary or organization-specific
Any mentions of specific third-party providers, rating agencies, or tools
Any year references or time-bound statements about enhancements or progress
Any role titles that are unique to the reference organization’s structure
Any detailed factor lists that could be interpreted as the reference company’s proprietary scoring model; instead, use generalized factor categories
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Names of business verticals and subsidiaries
Names/acronyms of internal frameworks, policies, and functions
References to specific external rating agencies and data providers
Mentions of specific roles and committees involved in approvals
Any explicit monitoring cadence and references to specific internal reporting artifacts
Religious/compliance product framing and its specific principle list (treated as content-specific rather than reusable wording)
